'''Ivan Wilkerson Johnson''' (born April 10, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Cisco College]], [[Los Angeles Southwest College|L.A. Southwest JC]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Cal State San Bernardino Coyotes|Cal State San Bernardino]].

Johnson is currently playing in the [[3x3 (basketball)|3-on-3]] basketball league [[BIG3]] playing for [[Ghost Ballers]].

==College career==
Johnson played college basketball for four different colleges, including two junior colleges, [[Cisco Junior College]] in Texas and [[Los Angeles Southwest College]], where he averaged 22.3 points, 12.2 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ivan Johnson – GoDucks.com – The University of Oregon Official Athletics Web Site|url=http://www.goducks.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=500&ATCLID=201188|access-date=May 28, 2012}}</ref>  He then transferred to the [[University of Oregon]] on a scholarship before finishing his college career at [[Cal State San Bernardino]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Browne|first=Rembert|title=Who Is Ivan Johnson And How'd He Wind Up With The Hawks? - From Our Editors - SBNation.com|url=http://www.grantland.com/blog/the-triangle/post/_/id/13431/where-has-ivan-johnson-been-all-our-lives|access-date=May 28, 2012}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===NBA D-League and Korean Basketball League (2007–2010)===
Johnson began his professional career in the [[NBA D-League]] where he played for the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] and [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] from 2007–2008. After that, he played in the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL) with the [[Changwon LG Sakers]] and [[Jeonju KCC Egis]] from 2008–2010. He was "banned forever" from the KBL for directing the [[finger (gesture)|middle-finger gesture]] at a referee during the final game of the championship series. After the game, the KBL held a meeting and also decided to fine Johnson US$4,448.<ref name="Korea Times">{{cite news | url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/sports/2011/01/136_64329.html | title=Ivan Johnson Banned From KBL Forever | newspaper=Korea Times | access-date=January 29, 2012}}</ref><ref name="sbnation" />

===Atlanta Hawks (2011–2012)===
On December 9, 2011, Johnson signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HAWKS: Hawks Re-Sign Jason Collins, Ink Tracy McGrady and Keith Benson|website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/training_camp_2011_pr.html|access-date=June 4, 2012}}</ref>  On April 13, 2012, Johnson was sent home and fined an undisclosed amount of money for "conduct detrimental to the team."<ref>{{cite news|last=Vivlamore|first=Chris|title=Update II: Ivan Johnson sent home|url=http://blogs.ajc.com/hawks/2012/04/13/breaking-news-ivan-johnson-sent-home/|newspaper=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|access-date=July 5, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120719183849/http://blogs.ajc.com/hawks/2012/04/13/breaking-news-ivan-johnson-sent-home/|archive-date=July 19, 2012}}</ref>  Just three days later on April 16, 2012, Johnson scored a career high 21 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ivan Johnson scored a career-high 21 points on 9-of-13 shooting|url=http://www.fantasysp.com/player/nba/Ivan_Johnson/2193914/ivan-johnson-scored-a-career-high-21-points-on-9-of-13-shooting|publisher=Rotoworld|access-date=June 4, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130122174655/http://www.fantasysp.com/player/nba/Ivan_Johnson/2193914/ivan-johnson-scored-a-career-high-21-points-on-9-of-13-shooting|archive-date=January 22, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Ivan Johnson Game Log">{{cite web|title=Ivan Johnson Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsiv01/gamelog/2012/|access-date=July 5, 2012}}</ref>

On May 12, 2012, the NBA fined Johnson $25,000 for gesturing, again with his middle finger, at a [[Boston Celtics]] fan following the Hawks’ elimination from the playoffs.<ref name="sbnation">{{cite web|last=Schroeder|first=Scott|title=PHOTO: Atlanta Hawks Get Eliminated, Ivan Johnson Uses Middle Finger Again - From Our Editors - SBNation.com|date=May 11, 2012 |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2012/5/11/3014108/ivan-johnson-middle-finger-photo|access-date=May 28, 2012}}</ref>

On September 18, 2012, Johnson signed a one-year deal to return to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].

===Zhejiang Golden Bulls (2013)===
In August 2013, Johnson signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] in China.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.zjczbc.com/news/clubnews/2013-08-29/862.html |title=关于稠州银行男篮正式签约伊万-约翰逊的公告 |access-date=August 29, 2013 |archive-date=October 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131028030158/http://www.zjczbc.com/news/clubnews/2013-08-29/862.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14145 |title=Ivan Johnson signs to play in China |access-date=August 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116135652/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14145 |archive-date=January 16, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Brief return to Dallas (2014)===
On July 29, 2014, Johnson signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/dallas-mavericks-sign-forward-ivan-johnson/|title=Dallas Mavericks sign forward Ivan Johnson|date=July 29, 2014|work=mavs.com|access-date=July 29, 2014}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Mavericks on October 25, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-waive-johnson-lamb-james/|title=Mavericks request waivers on Bernard James, Ivan Johnson and Doron Lamb|work=mavs.com|date=October 25, 2014|access-date=October 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025223720/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-waive-johnson-lamb-james/|archive-date=October 25, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 5, 2014, he was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_acquire_ivan_johnson.html Legends Acquire Ivan Johnson] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210175935/http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_acquire_ivan_johnson.html |date=February 10, 2015 }}</ref> On February 6, 2015, he was waived by Texas.<ref>[http://dleague.nba.com/news/transactions/ NBA D-League 2014–15 Transactions] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626110843/http://dleague.nba.com/news/transactions/ |date=June 26, 2015 }}</ref>

===Talk 'N Text (2015)===
On February 18, 2015, Johnson signed with [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Atlanta Hawk Ivan Johnson replaces Richard Howell on Talk 'N Text|url=https://www.rappler.com/sports/pba/84240-richard-howell-replaced-talk-n-text-import/|work=rappler.com|date=February 18, 2015|access-date=February 18, 2015}}</ref> On April 29, 2015, he helped the Texters to win the [[2015 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Talk N' Text withstands Rain or Shine in 2OT, nabs PBA Commissioner's Cup title|url=http://sports.inquirer.net/179626/talk-n-text-withstands-rain-or-shine-in-2ot-nabs-pba-commissioners-cup-title|work=INQUIRER.net|date=April 29, 2015|access-date=April 29, 2015}}</ref>

===RETAbet.es GBC (2015)===
In September 2015, Johnson signed with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|RETAbet.es GBC]] of Spain for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gigantes.com/retabet-es-gbc-cierra-plantilla-con-el-polemico-interior-ivan-johnson/|title=RETAbet.es GBC cierra plantilla con el polémico interior Ivan Johnson|language=es|publisher=Gigantes del Basket|date=September 15, 2015|access-date=September 15, 2015|archive-date=September 19, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919145515/http://www.gigantes.com/retabet-es-gbc-cierra-plantilla-con-el-polemico-interior-ivan-johnson/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Though, in October he had to leave the team.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Carchia|first1=E.|title=Gipuzkoa coach Ponsarnau confirms Ivan Johnson will be waived|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/177900/gipuzkoa-coach-ponsarnau-confirms-ivan-johnson-will-be-waived.html|website=Sportando.com|access-date=October 6, 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Talk 'N Text / Tropang TNT (2016)===
On January 13, 2016, Johnson signed once again with the defending champion [[Tropang TNT]] as the team's import for the [[2016 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ivan Johnson returns to re-energize Texters|url=http://www.philstar.com/sports/2016/01/13/1542197/ivan-johnson-returns-re-energize-texters|publisher= Richard Dy, philstar.com|date=January 13, 2016|access-date=January 17, 2016}}</ref> Days before the Commissioner's Cup, he was figured in a brawl with two players of Blackwater Elite in the team's tune-up game in Moro Lorenzo Gym. Johnson was suspended for one game and fined 50,000 pesos after the incident.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/ivan-johnson-suspended-one-game-slapped-p50000-fine-for-fight-in-blackwater-tuneup|title=TNT import Ivan Johnson suspended one game, fined P50,000 for fight in tune-up. |publisher=Spin.ph|author=Badua, Snow|author-link=Snow Badua|date=February 3, 2016|access-date=February 3, 2016}}</ref>

On February 13, 2016, Johnson was "banned for life" from the [[Philippine Basketball Association|PBA]] and fined 250,000 pesos after he disrespected and cursed the PBA commissioner [[Chito Narvasa]] during their game against [[Meralco Bolts]], earlier in the game he was called for a technical foul for second motion on Meralco's [[Forward-center|Forward/Center]] [[Kelly Nabong]] and a flagrant foul one penalty after he gave an elbow to the face of Meralco's Forward/Center [[Bryan Faundo]] and his second technical foul came from his encounter with the commissioner Narvasa that led him to be ejected from the game.<ref>{{cite web|title=TNT import Ivan Johnson fined P250k, banned from PBA|url=http://pba.inquirer.net/67139/tnt-import-ivan-johnson-fined-p250k-banned-from-pba|publisher=INQUIRER.net|date=February 13, 2016|access-date=February 13, 2016}}</ref>

Johnson, through his [[Twitter]] account, later apologized to Commissioner Narvasa and thanked the PBA for giving him the chance to return as the import of the [[Tropang TNT]] for the second consecutive time.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/story/555225/sports/boxing/pba-ivan-johnson-apologizes-to-commissioner-narvasa-after-lifetime-ban|title=PBA: Ivan Johnson apologizes to Commissioner Narvasa after lifetime ban|publisher=GMA News|last=Panaligan|first=Marisse|date=February 14, 2016|access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref> In a press conference, Narvasa accepted Johnson's apology, three days after the incident.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hoops.ph/pba-commissioner-chito-narvasa-accepts-ivan-johnsons-apology/|title=PBA Commissioner Chito Narvasa accepts Ivan Johnson's apology|publisher=Hoops.ph|date=February 15, 2016|access-date=February 15, 2016|archive-date=February 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160218010955/http://hoops.ph/pba-commissioner-chito-narvasa-accepts-ivan-johnsons-apology/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The PBA later downgraded the ban order to a suspension good for one season and the fine has been reduced to 150,000 pesos.<ref>{{cite news|title=Basketball: Ex-NBA player's Philippines life ban reduced|url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/sport/basketball-ex-nba-player/2522862.html|access-date=February 17, 2016|agency=AFP|publisher=Channel NewsAsia|date=February 17, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160217190108/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/sport/basketball-ex-nba-player/2522862.html|archive-date=February 17, 2016}}</ref>

===Petrochimi Bandar Imam / Caciques de Humacao (2016)===
On March 9, 2016, Johnson signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Petrochimi signs Hamed Haddadi and Ivan Johnson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/193592/petrochimi-signs-hamed-haddadi-and-ivan-johnson.html|work=Sportando.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> However, he never played for the Iranian team. On April 25, he left Petrochimi and signed with Caciques de Humacao for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luis|last=Modestti|title=Caciques firman a Ivan Johnson|url=http://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=10194#.Vx7Nw6MrKRs|work=BSNpr.com|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016|language=es|archive-date=September 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180916164301/https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=10194#.Vx7Nw6MrKRs|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Hekmeh/Sagesse (2016)===
On December 12, 2016, Johnson signed with [[Hekmeh BC|Sagesse]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].

===Alab Pilipinas (2017)===
After a stint in the [[BIG3]], Johnson returned to professional, 5-on-5 basketball after being signed by the [[Alab Pilipinas]] of the [[ASEAN Basketball League]] as its new World Import.<ref>{{ cite news |last=Riego |first=Norman Lee Benjamin |title=Johnson joins, Domingo returns for Alab Pilipinas |url=http://sports.abs-cbn.com/basketball/news/2017/09/19/johnson-joins-domingo-returns-alab-pilipinas-31148 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922104628/http://sports.abs-cbn.com/basketball/news/2017/09/19/johnson-joins-domingo-returns-alab-pilipinas-31148 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 22, 2017 |work=[[ABS-CBN News]] |date=September 19, 2017 |access-date=September 19, 2017 }}</ref><ref>[https://m.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=1882291792098861&substory_index=0&id=1680871328907576 Alab Pilipinas NEW World Import, Ivan Johnson!]</ref> This will be Johnson's third stint playing in the Philippines.
